selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Retirement Fairness for Charities and Educational Institutions Act of 2025 amends federal securities laws to allow 403(b) retirement plans—which are typically used by employees of public schools, charities, and churches—to invest in bank-maintained collective investment trusts and insurance company separate accounts under specific conditions.

affected_groups.effect: Gain access to collective investment trusts and insurance company separate accounts in their retirement plans if specific employer, fiduciary, or review conditions are met.
Must meet specific conditions, such as agreeing to serve as a plan fiduciary for investment selection or reviewing and approving investment alternatives, depending on the plan type.

key_provisions: Amends the Investment Company Act of 1940 to allow 403(b) plans to include collective trust funds maintained by banks, provided certain fiduciary or review requirements are met.
Amends the Investment Company Act of 1940 to permit 403(b) plan assets to be derived from insurance company separate accounts.
Amends the Securities Act of 1933 regarding 403(b) plans that are subject to ERISA, involve employer agreement to serve as an investment fiduciary, or are governmental plans.
Amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to update exemptions and definitions to incorporate qualifying 403(b) plans.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Retirement Fairness for Charities and Educational Institutions Act of 2025 amends federal securities laws to allow 403(b) retirement plans—which are typically used by employees of public schools, charities, and churches—to invest in bank-maintained collective investment trusts and insurance company separate accounts under specific conditions.
summary_detail.significance: The bill adjusts federal securities laws to align 403(b) retirement investment options more closely with other retirement plan types by permitting collective investment trusts and insurance company separate accounts.
